title: High-risk sites split into 2 distinct risk fingerprints
finding: Clustering the 96 sites by their observed pathogen/faecal/ARG profile reveals 2 groups with genuinely different risk shapes — a single composite score would blur these together.
limitation: Clusters describe observed risk composition only; they do not explain why a site has that profile, and k is chosen by silhouette, not theory.
next_step: Profile each cluster against land-use and season with repeated sampling.

challenge.detail: Permutation test: real silhouette 0.380 vs random 0.278 (95th pct 0.337); p=0.010. Structure is stronger than chance.

title: Vegetation fragmentation within 250 m tracks stream health risk
finding: Across 96 sites, vegetation fragmentation within 250 m shows a positive rank association with composite risk (Spearman rho = +0.28).
limitation: Cross-sectional, single sample per site; association is not causation and effect sizes are small.
next_step: Re-test with within-city controls and repeated seasonal sampling.

challenge.detail: Within-city (city effect removed): rho = +0.18 (p=0.078); global rho = +0.28. Sign consistent in 5/5 cities. Association survives after controlling for city.

title: Distance to wastewater stations tracks stream health risk
finding: Across 96 sites, distance to wastewater stations shows a negative rank association with composite risk (Spearman rho = -0.22).
limitation: Cross-sectional, single sample per site; association is not causation and effect sizes are small.
next_step: Re-test with within-city controls and repeated seasonal sampling.

challenge.detail: Within-city (city effect removed): rho = -0.23 (p=0.021); global rho = -0.22. Sign consistent in 4/5 cities. Association survives after controlling for city.

challenge.detail: Within-city (city effect removed): rho = -0.25 (p=0.015); global rho = -0.20. Sign consistent in 3/5 cities. Association survives after controlling for city.

title: Composite score hides a dominant risk dimension at some sites
finding: 6 sites have one risk component at least 0.35 above their composite score — the average masks a substantially elevated dimension.
limitation: Reflects how the composite is defined (mean of three components); descriptive.
next_step: Report and triage by dominant component, not by composite alone.

challenge.detail: Arithmetic fact about the observed components, not a modelled claim — robust by construction.

title: A few sites stand well above their own city's norm
finding: 9 sites sit at least 1.5 standard deviations above their city's mean composite risk — local hotspots worth first inspection.

examples: C5 (Coimbra): +2.6 SD above its city mean (composite 0.78)
BN2 (Benevento): +2.6 SD above its city mean (composite 0.73)
G9 (Ghent): +2.4 SD above its city mean (composite 0.36)
O17 (Oslo): +1.9 SD above its city mean (composite 0.42)
BN10 (Benevento): +1.9 SD above its city mean (composite 0.62)

limitation: Based on one sample per site; an outlier may reflect sampling, not a trend.
next_step: Re-sample flagged sites and their upstream/downstream neighbours.

challenge.detail: Descriptive within-city ranking; not a cross-city or predictive claim.

title: Some high-risk sites are NOT explained by the trusted patterns
finding: 3 high-risk sites have a benign environment on both patterns that survived the challenge — low vegetation fragmentation and far from wastewater. The known environmental story does not account for their risk.

examples: BN4 (Benevento): composite 0.38, 0.1 fragmentation, 6.7 km from wastewater
BN15 (Benevento): composite 0.37, 0.0 fragmentation, 11.7 km from wastewater
T6 (Toulouse): composite 0.36, 0.2 fragmentation, 5.4 km from wastewater

limitation: A single sample per site; the mismatch could be sampling noise or an unmeasured local source (e.g. upstream discharge).
next_step: Prioritise these for repeat sampling and an upstream source search — they are where the environmental model is least able to help.

challenge.detail: These sites are defined by breaking the surviving associations, so they are hypothesis-generating investigation candidates, not a predictive claim. Robust as a flag; the cause is unknown.

title: Most citizen submissions need review before they can be trusted
finding: 56 of 71 citizen submissions (79%) are flagged: 10 junk names, 19 duplicates, 1 swapped coordinates, 30 out of region.
limitation: Swap detection only catches swaps that land in a partner country; other swaps show as out-of-region.
next_step: Prompt citizens to confirm flagged coordinates and merge duplicate points at capture time.

challenge.detail: Deterministic rule outcomes on the actual submissions — fully reproducible.

title: Composite risk differs significantly across cities
finding: City ranking by mean composite risk: Benevento (0.34) > Coimbra (0.33) > Toulouse (0.31) > Oslo (0.28) > Ghent (0.23).
limitation: City differences may reflect sampling protocol, season or land-use, not water quality alone.
next_step: Model with a city random effect before comparing environmental drivers across cities.

challenge.detail: Kruskal-Wallis p=0.060. Not clearly beyond chance.

challenge.detail: Within-city (city effect removed): rho = -0.06 (p=0.535); global rho = -0.22. Sign consistent in 3/5 cities. Association largely reflects differences BETWEEN cities, not within them — weakened.
